editorial_policy: Keep the original historical shelf open; do not turn six windows into a national ranking or inevitable ladder. No invented scenes, dialogue, private motive or composite claimant. English is independently written; both Chinese scripts preserve the complete argument.
checked_distinctions: England: February 13 declaration accompanied the offer of the Crown, not a modern conditional contract; December 16 statutory enactment is separate. The official catalogue's 1688 date does not override the 1689 assent note.
England: an invading army, a Convention not summoned in the usual royal manner, and the violence in Ireland/Scotland are not erased by a bloodless or purely legal narrative.
England: parliamentary speech privilege is not universal speech freedom; free elections do not imply equal adult suffrage; conditional Protestant toleration does not include Catholic equality.

England: three-year maximum parliamentary duration is distinguished from annual elections and from present-day law; parliamentary revenue control may coexist with greater state capacity and discriminatory taxation.
Pakistan: July 20, 2007 judicial reinstatement differs from the November exclusion and March 2009 executive restoration; no private motive is asserted solely from proximity to eligibility litigation.
Pakistan: the October interim order permitted the election while withholding the final return notification; it did not cancel the election or finally disqualify Musharraf.

Pakistan: the Chief of Army Staff issued proclamation/PCO; the oath order was issued as President. Not every existing judge received an identical opportunity to swear; no universal inference about individual motives follows from oath status.
Pakistan: the November 3 seven-judge restraint existed but did not prevent exclusion; the later invalidity ruling does not retroactively supply effective protection in 2007.
Pakistan: March 16 announcement, March 17 notification and March 22 resumption are distinct; the July 31 short order is distinguished from the judgment's later detailed reasons.

Pakistan: the judgment preserved other litigants' ordinary decisions and specified administrative/financial acts rather than voiding every intervening act; restoration does not certify every later judicial decision.
source_access_notes: The original Bill of Rights text on legislation.gov.uk returned application/xhtml+xml unsupported by the web parser. Its actual HTML was retrieved and read separately, including the original enacted version and assent note.
The old g03 parliamentary factsheet returned 404. The published citation instead uses the accessible Commons Library RP10/54 historical sections 4.2 and 4.5; no dead factsheet is published.

Two UK Parliament historical pages retain outdated present-tense claims about Catholic-spouse succession and a reigning queen. Only their historical facts are used and the limitation is disclosed in reader notes.

The ecoi.net reproduction explicitly includes November 15 amendments. The essay does not backdate the new amendment power to November 3; sections 2–4 used are continuing provisions. Its 5007 date typo is disclosed.

The July 2007 Supreme Court press-release link linked by JURIST was unavailable. The contemporary Library of Congress report and primary 2009 judgment mirror are used with clear provenance, not represented as official-host authentication.

The Lahore bar account is a participant institution's retrospective history. Arrest totals and restrictions are attributed to the contemporary International Commission of Jurists, not presented as an exhaustive verified census.
